questions.stem: The upper B cell receives antigen (Signal 1) plus T-cell help through CD40L-CD40 (Signal 2) and secretes antibody, whereas the lower B cell receives only Signal 1 and becomes unresponsive. Why is this two-signal requirement immunologically important?

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is required for the B cell to fix complement

choices.label: D
choices.text: It restricts class switching exclusively to IgE

choices.label: E
choices.text: It enforces self-tolerance, preventing B cells from responding to self-antigen without T-cell help

explanation.summary: A B cell engaging antigen without a second signal from a helper T cell becomes anergic. Requiring T-cell help for full activation is a peripheral tolerance checkpoint that limits autoantibody production.
explanation.whyCorrect: A B cell engaging antigen without a second signal from a helper T cell becomes anergic. Requiring T-cell help for full activation is a peripheral tolerance checkpoint that limits autoantibody production.

questions.stem: This figure shows developing thymocytes selected by how strongly their TCR binds self-peptide-MHC. Failure of the top pathway (strong self-antigen binding) would MOST likely result in:

choices.label: C
choices.text: Autoimmunity, because self-reactive T cells escape deletion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inability to recognize any MHC molecule

explanation.summary: Thymocytes binding self strongly undergo negative selection (apoptosis). Loss of this deletion allows autoreactive T cells into the periphery, predisposing to autoimmune disease. Weak binding gives positive selection; intermediate binding can yield Tregs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thymocytes binding self strongly undergo negative selection (apoptosis). Loss of this deletion allows autoreactive T cells into the periphery, predisposing to autoimmune disease. Weak binding gives positive selection; intermediate binding can yield Tregs.

questions.stem: In this bone-marrow figure, a self-reactive immature B cell that strongly binds self-antigen follows pathway A. Which tolerance mechanism does pathway A represent?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clonal deletion (apoptosis) of the self-reactive B cell

explanation.summary: Immature B cells strongly engaging self-antigen in the marrow are removed by apoptosis (clonal deletion), a central-tolerance mechanism. Alternatively they may rearrange the light chain (receptor editing) to change specificity, shown by the other pathways.
explanation.whyCorrect: Immature B cells strongly engaging self-antigen in the marrow are removed by apoptosis (clonal deletion), a central-tolerance mechanism. Alternatively they may rearrange the light chain (receptor editing) to change specificity, shown by the other pathways.

questions.stem: The antibody shown being transported across the intestinal epithelium into the lumen neutralizes microbes without provoking inflammation. In what form is it secreted to resist luminal proteolysis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A secretory dimer joined by a J chain and bearing secretory component

explanation.summary: Secretory IgA is a dimer linked by a J chain; transcytosis adds the secretory component, which protects it from proteases in the gut lumen. It provides noninflammatory mucosal defense against commensal and pathogenic microbes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Secretory IgA is a dimer linked by a J chain; transcytosis adds the secretory component, which protects it from proteases in the gut lumen. It provides noninflammatory mucosal defense against commensal and pathogenic microbes.

questions.stem: The central cell suppresses effector T cells partly by expressing high levels of CD25 to capture IL-2 (in addition to IL-10/TGF-beta, CTLA-4/B7, and cytolysis). How does high CD25 expression inhibit effector T cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It delivers costimulation to effector T cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: It consumes IL-2, depriving effector T cells of the growth factor they need to proliferate and survive

choices.label: C
choices.text: It upregulates B7 on dendritic cells

explanation.summary: Regulatory T cells constitutively express the high-affinity IL-2 receptor (CD25) and act as an IL-2 sink, starving nearby effector T cells of IL-2. They also suppress via IL-10/TGF-beta, CTLA-4 competition for B7, and granzyme/perforin cytolysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Regulatory T cells constitutively express the high-affinity IL-2 receptor (CD25) and act as an IL-2 sink, starving nearby effector T cells of IL-2. They also suppress via IL-10/TGF-beta, CTLA-4 competition for B7, and granzyme/perforin cytolysis.

questions.stem: The upper T cell receives TCR-MHC (signal 1) plus B7-CD28 costimulation (signal 2) and proliferates, whereas the lower T cell gets signal 1 only and becomes unresponsive. Blocking B7-CD28 costimulation (e.g., with CTLA-4-Ig) would therefore:

choices.label: C
choices.text: Induce T-cell anergy and dampen the immune response

explanation.summary: Full T-cell activation requires antigen recognition plus B7-CD28 costimulation. Antigen without costimulation induces anergy, a peripheral-tolerance mechanism. CTLA-4-Ig blocks B7, so it suppresses T-cell responses (used therapeutically in autoimmunity/transplant).
explanation.whyCorrect: Full T-cell activation requires antigen recognition plus B7-CD28 costimulation. Antigen without costimulation induces anergy, a peripheral-tolerance mechanism. CTLA-4-Ig blocks B7, so it suppresses T-cell responses (used therapeutically in autoimmunity/transplant).

questions.stem: The cell on the right kills its target using granules containing perforin and granzymes (as well as Fas-FasL). A patient with a mutation causing nonfunctional perforin would have MOST impaired ability to:

choices.label: B
choices.text: Degranulate mast cells in allergic responses

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kill virus-infected and tumor cells via CD8+ T cells and NK cells

explanation.summary: Perforin lets granzymes enter target cells to trigger apoptosis, the core cytotoxic mechanism of CD8+ CTLs and NK cells. Loss-of-function causes impaired cytotoxicity (e.g., familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis).
explanation.whyCorrect: Perforin lets granzymes enter target cells to trigger apoptosis, the core cytotoxic mechanism of CD8+ CTLs and NK cells. Loss-of-function causes impaired cytotoxicity (e.g., familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis).
